questions.answer: I wouldn't say many, but I have a small circle I really trust. I've always preferred a few close friendships over a wide range of [[acquaintances]]. Those are the people I can be completely myself around.

questions.q: How did you meet your closest friends?
questions.answer: Most of them are from school and university, so we've known each other for years and share a lot of history. A couple are former colleagues too, which shows that friendships can [[blossom]] in unexpected places.

questions.q: Can you describe your best friend?
questions.answer: Sure. He's easygoing, genuinely kind and a great listener, which is probably why we've stayed close for so long. He has this [[reassuring]] way of putting things in perspective whenever I'm stressed.

questions.q: What do you usually do with your friends?
questions.answer: Nothing too elaborate. We usually meet at a local tea stall and chat for hours, or watch a cricket match together. Sometimes we take a walk by the river. It's the easy, [[unpretentious]] company that I value most.

questions.q: Do you think it's easy to make friends as an adult?
questions.answer: Not as easy as it was at school. Adults are busy with work and family, so there are fewer chances to connect naturally. Friendships still form, but they take more time and [[deliberate]] effort.
